assessmentSummary.identity: Stand with the back to a stable wall, use available head, upper-back, hip, and heel contacts without forcing unavailable contact, lightly brace, raise both arms overhead without rib flare, hold the declared alignment, step away, then recall the same line. It is not a wall handstand, wall slide, wall sit, loaded overhead mobility drill, posture assessment, or clinical intervention.
currentCardFindings: Source 77 supplies an ordered standing wall-contact, overhead-reach, and recall sequence but omits a count unit, contact policy, dosage, fatigue, safety, alternates, and review contracts.
The exact card must make contact availability an observation rather than a force target; forcing head, heel, or lumbar contact changes the task and could create a false quality standard.
One search result is standing wall reach; three handstand body-line results are adjacent-only and remain unverified, non-embedded candidates.

currentCardSnapshot.description: Stand with the back to a stable wall. Use available head, upper-back, hip, and heel contacts without forcing unavailable contact, brace lightly, raise both arms overhead without rib flare, hold the declared alignment, step away, and recall the same line. One wall-contact reach-and-recall is one cycle. Wall handstands, wall slides, wall sits, forced contact, loaded reach, assessment, and clinical interventions are separate tasks.
